scope: Theorem 1.3 (Regularity of a phase-foliated collar) of the manuscript “Continuous Phase Foliations Create Analytic Caustic Collars” (preprints/Continuous-Phase-Foliations-Create-Analytic-Caustic-Collars-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 147 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 357beeb0c0854e26), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, the boundary is real analytic. There are λ0 > 0 and a jointly real-analytic map Γ : T × [0, λ0] −→ R2 such that Γ(·, 0) parametrizes ∂Ω, every curve Γ(·, λ) for 0 < λ ≤ λ0 is a regular strictly convex caustic, and the restriction to T × [0, λ0) is a homeomorphism onto a relatively open collar of ∂Ω in Ω. Here real analyticity at the parameter endpoints means extension to a neighborhood.
